cues.en: I've lived in Amsterdam for over a year and a half now, and it occurred to me the other day that I haven't seen a car crash into a building yet.
cues.zh: 我在阿姆斯特丹住了超过一年半，前几天我突然意识到，我还没见过汽车撞进建筑的事故。

cues.en: It's not that cars never crash into buildings in The Netherlands, but it is exceedingly rare. And I hadn't seen it or heard of it happening until I went looking for articles about it.
cues.zh: 并不是说荷兰的汽车从不撞进建筑，而是这种事极其罕见。在我主动搜索相关文章之前，我既没见过也没听说过。

cues.en: When we were living in Toronto, my son's preschool was here.
cues.zh: 我们住在多伦多时，我儿子的幼儿园就在这里。

cues.en: One day, we noticed a car had smashed into the drugstore here,
cues.zh: 有一天，我们注意到一辆车撞进了这里的药店，

cues.en: a place that we walked every day because the streetcar stop was here.
cues.zh: 那是我们每天都会走过的地方，因为电车站就在这儿。

cues.en: A few weeks later, a car smashed into a pizza shop here on the other side of his preschool.
cues.zh: 几周后，一辆车撞进了幼儿园另一侧的一家披萨店。

cues.en: Incidentally,
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，

cues.en: around the same time, a speeding SUV ran a red light and knocked over a school bus a few blocks away. But that doesn't count here because a school bus is not a building.
cues.zh: 差不多同一时期，一辆超速的SUV闯了红灯，在几个街区外撞翻了一辆校车。但这不算数，因为校车不是建筑。

cues.en: Cars crashing into buildings is pretty common in The US and Canada.
cues.zh: 汽车撞进建筑在美国和加拿大相当常见。

cues.en: Good evening. It's a dramatic scene and the third call for a car smashing into a home in a single day.
cues.zh: 晚上好。现场画面很惊险，这是当天第三起汽车撞进住宅的报警。

cues.en: In Toronto, cars crash into buildings so often that in many cases, it doesn't even make the news.
cues.zh: 在多伦多，汽车撞进建筑太频繁了，很多时候甚至上不了新闻。

cues.en: I tried to search for a news article about the drugstore by my son's preschool.
cues.zh: 我试着搜索关于我儿子幼儿园旁边那家药店的新闻报道。

cues.en: I couldn't find it.
cues.zh: 没找到。

cues.en: But I did find an article about a car crashing into this shopper's drug mart, and this one,
cues.zh: 但我确实找到了一篇关于一辆车撞进这家Shopper's Drug Mart的文章，还有这一篇，

cues.en: and this one,
cues.zh: 还有这一篇，

cues.en: and this one, and this one, this and and this one, one, and this one.
cues.zh: 还有这一篇、这一篇、这一篇、这一篇、这一篇，还有这一篇。

cues.en: In fact, the only place I found any information at all was in this Reddit post by someone who saw it.
cues.zh: 实际上，我唯一能找到相关信息的地方，就是Reddit上有人目睹后发的帖子。

cues.en: The news did report on the pizza store crash though, so there's that.
cues.zh: 不过新闻确实报道了那家披萨店被撞的事件，至少还有这个。

cues.en: Now a lot of people in Canada and in The US brush this stuff off by saying, it was some old person that mixed up the brake pedal and the gas pedal, or a drunk driver,
cues.zh: 现在加拿大和美国的很多人对这类事情不以为然，说不过是某个老人把刹车踏板和油门踏板搞混了，或者是醉驾司机，

cues.en: or maybe they'll say it was due to bad weather.
cues.zh: 或者他们可能会说是天气不好导致的。

cues.en: Now ignoring city design that forces everyone, even very old people, to have to drive everywhere,
cues.zh: 先不说城市规划迫使每个人——甚至包括上了年纪的老人——去哪都得开车，

cues.en: the truth is a lot of these crashes are in the middle of the day in clear weather by regular drivers,
cues.zh: 事实是，很多这类事故都发生在白天、天气晴朗的时候，肇事者是普通司机，

cues.en: and a common factor is speed.
cues.zh: 而一个共同因素是速度。

cues.en: North American roads are designed to be wide and straight.
cues.zh: 北美的道路设计得又宽又直。

cues.en: They weren't always built like that, but over time, roads were widened and straightened in the name of safety
cues.zh: 它们并非一直都是这样建的，但随着时间的推移，道路以安全之名被拓宽和拉直，

cues.en: for drivers.
cues.zh: 是为了司机的安全。

cues.en: Unfortunately,
cues.zh: 不幸的是，

cues.en: we now know that wide straight roads make people drive faster.
cues.zh: 我们现在知道，又宽又直的道路会让人开得更快。

cues.en: And when you remove complexity from the street, like removing trees and putting buildings farther away, it's harder to judge your speed by your surroundings.
cues.zh: 而当你去掉街道上的复杂性时，比如移除树木、把建筑建得更远，你就更难通过周围环境来判断自己的车速。

cues.en: So in this kind of environment, almost every driver drives really fast without even thinking about it.
cues.zh: 所以在这种环境里，几乎每个司机都会开得飞快，甚至想都不去想。

cues.en: When living in Toronto, I remember seeing this tweet from the police.
cues.zh: 住在多伦多的时候，我记得看到过警方发的这条推文。

cues.en: Ignoring why any street by a school would have a 50 kilometer per hour speed limit, why is it even physically possible to drive over a 100 kilometers an hour down this street?
cues.zh: 先不说为什么学校旁边的街道限速会是每小时50公里，为什么这条街上竟然在物理上可能开到每小时100公里以上？

cues.en: But seeing drivers going double the speed limit was literally a daily occurrence for us in Toronto. It has become completely normalized.
cues.zh: 但在多伦多，我们看到司机超速一倍简直是家常便饭。这已经完全常态化了。

cues.en: Incidentally,
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，

cues.en: after the nineteen sixties, roads became wide and straight in The Netherlands too. But a few decades later, Dutch cities realized their mistake and purposely narrowed streets to increase safety.
cues.zh: 上世纪六十年代之后，荷兰的道路也变得又宽又直。但几十年后，荷兰城市意识到了自己的错误，特意缩窄街道以提高安全性。

cues.en: Bicycle Dutch has a fantastic video about this that I'll link to in the description.
cues.zh: Bicycle Dutch 有一个很棒的相关视频，我会把链接放在简介里。

cues.en: Everybody should watch it.
cues.zh: 大家都应该看看。

cues.en: So wide straight roads increase vehicle speeds, and an increase in speeds turns what would normally be a small crash or maybe no crash at all into this.
cues.zh: 所以又宽又直的道路会提高车速，而车速的提高会把原本只是小碰撞、甚至根本不会发生的事故变成这样。

cues.en: Now the other difference is that in The Netherlands, if there's a serious crash, the road is closed and there's an investigation as to why the crash happened and what might be done to prevent it.
cues.zh: 另一个区别是，在荷兰，如果发生严重事故，道路会被封闭，并调查事故原因以及可以采取什么措施来预防。

cues.en: In Canada, they clean up the mess and that's it. There will be a police investigation for insurance purposes, but nothing will be done about the road.
cues.zh: 在加拿大，他们清理完现场就完事了。会有警方出于保险目的的调查，但不会对道路做任何处理。

cues.en: There's a cultural element to this. In English speaking countries, there's a big emphasis on personal
cues.zh: 这其中有文化因素。在英语国家，非常强调个人

cues.en: responsibility.
cues.zh: 责任。

cues.en: When a crash happens, the discussion immediately jumps to which person is at fault.
cues.zh: 事故发生时，讨论立刻就会跳到是谁的过错。

cues.en: And especially
cues.zh: 尤其是

cues.en: when people are hit by cars,
cues.zh: 当人们被车撞到的时候，

cues.en: victim blaming is very common.
cues.zh: 受害者有罪论非常普遍。

cues.en: That person clearly must have done something wrong to get hit by a car.
cues.zh: 那个人肯定做错了什么才会被车撞到。

cues.en: So when a building gets hit by a car, it's always fun to make the same arguments.
cues.zh: 所以当一栋建筑被车撞到时，用同样的论点来调侃总是很有意思。

cues.en: That house must have been looking at their phone,
cues.zh: 那栋房子肯定一直在看手机，

cues.en: or
cues.zh: 或者

cues.en: that drugstore shouldn't have been wearing dark clothing,
cues.zh: 那家药店不该穿深色衣服，

cues.en: or if the building had a reflective vest and some lights, this never would have happened.
cues.zh: 或者如果那栋楼穿了反光背心、装了些灯，这事根本就不会发生。

cues.en: The approach taken by The Netherlands and some other countries like Sweden is very different.
cues.zh: 荷兰和瑞典等一些国家的做法则截然不同。

cues.en: They say that road crashes are preventable.
cues.zh: 他们认为道路交通事故是可以预防的。

cues.en: Humans are imperfect and they make mistakes,
cues.zh: 人并不完美，会犯错，

cues.en: so road infrastructure should be designed so that those mistakes don't result in serious injury.
cues.zh: 所以道路基础设施的设计应当确保这些错误不会导致严重伤害。

cues.en: That results in things like
cues.zh: 这就带来了诸如

cues.en: separating different types of traffic,
cues.zh: 分离不同类型的交通，

cues.en: narrowing roads and adding complexity to get people to drive slower,
cues.zh: 收窄道路并增加复杂度以促使人们减速行驶，

cues.en: restricting car traffic to residents only,
cues.zh: 限制汽车交通仅限居民通行，

cues.en: and many other different kinds of traffic calming.
cues.zh: 以及许多其他不同类型的交通稳静化措施。

cues.en: There can be wide straight roads here too.
cues.zh: 这里也可以有宽阔笔直的道路。

cues.en: But when you get into the city, the infrastructure changes.
cues.zh: 但当你进入市区，基础设施就变了。

cues.en: And when a crash does happen, the investigation includes the actions of the driver, of course, but also what could change about the infrastructure to prevent a similar crash in the future.
cues.zh: 而当事故真的发生时，调查当然包括驾驶员的行为，但也包括基础设施可以做出哪些改变，以预防未来发生类似事故。

cues.en: The roads in The Netherlands were designed this way on purpose, and they haven't always been this way. A lot of this change only started in the nineties.
cues.zh: 荷兰的道路是故意这样设计的，而且它们并非一直如此。很多这样的改变直到九十年代才开始。

cues.en: These roads came about by putting victim blaming and finger pointing aside and focusing on the street itself and how to make it safer.
cues.zh: 这些道路的出现，靠的是把受害者有罪论和互相指责放到一边，专注于街道本身以及如何让它更安全。

cues.en: The end result is a city that's a lot more comfortable to be in, especially when you're outside of a vehicle. And for us, that results in a better quality of life.
cues.zh: 最终的结果是一座住起来舒适得多的城市，尤其是当你不在车里的时候。对我们来说，这带来了更好的生活质量。

cues.en: And I don't know about you, but I'm pretty happy living somewhere where cars
cues.zh: 我不知道你怎么想，但我挺高兴自己住的地方，汽车

cues.en: generally aren't crashing into buildings.
cues.zh: 一般不会撞进建筑物里。
